subject: [RFC PATCH 0/5] mm: sub-folio dirty tracking for PTE-mapped mmap writes

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a mistake in the page_vma_mkclean_one() function and provided a fixup patch to correct it, indicating that the issue will be addressed in the next version of the patch (v2).

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: The author acknowledged a concern about the clearing of PG_reclaim and PG_readahead flags in folio_mark_dirty() and folio_mark_dirty_range(), agreed to move the clearing into mapping_dirty_range(), which is the correct place for it, and confirmed that this fix will be folded into v2.

2026-09-10.patch_summary: This patch set introduces sub-folio dirty tracking for PTE-mapped mmap writes, addressing the issue of large page cache folios being dirtied unnecessarily when a single byte is written through a shared file mapping. The problem arises because current implementations mark the entire folio as dirty, leading to inefficient writeback and increased minor fault counts. To solve this, the patch harvests hardware PTE dirty bits at page_mkwrite() time and provides the filesystem with the ranges that were actually modified, allowing for more targeted writeback. This approach is already implemented in XFS and is shown to reduce writeback by 99% on a large file system.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
reviews.summary: Raised a concern that the current implementation may not be suitable for large folio adoption, suggesting consideration of alternative approaches to improve performance.

reviews.author: Matthew Wilcox
reviews.summary: Proposed an alternative solution that involves calling page_mkwrite() for each page fault, allowing filesystems to track dirty pages without relying on the PTL.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, Sep 16, 2026 at 06:09:17PM +0100, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> On Wed, Sep 16, 2026 at 05:27:42PM +0100, Matthew Wilcox wrote:
> > On Mon, Sep 07, 2026 at 11:15:15AM +0100, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> > > My proposal makes the distinction between making the folio writable and
> > > making it dirty meaningful. ->page_mkwrite() allocates whatever is needed
> > > on the filesystem side to track dirty state and drive writeback for the
> > > *folio*, while ->dirty_folio_range() marks part of the folio dirty.
> > 
> > Why do you think that's a meaningful distinction?  We create a writable
> > PTE because we've taken a page fault for write.  There's probably a few
> > naoseconds where the PTE is writable+clean before it becomes
> > writable+dirty, but even then sometimes we do both pte_mkwrite() and
> > pte_mkdirty() as an optimisation in the write fault path.
> 
> This is true for the PTE that the fault was for. But we don't necessarily
> want to dirty the other 511 pages at the same time.
> 
> The basic idea is to make the whole folio writable at fault and shift
> dirtying to be per-PTE on write to it.

Hmm.  Is that something that filesystem people want?  I suspect not.
I think they'd prefer to be told when we write-fault on each page.
But let's see if we can gather feedback from FS people.

> > It's very odd to be optimising for shared-writable-mmap.  This is a
> > horrid model for I/O.  https://cs.brown.edu/people/acrotty/pubs/p13-crotty.pdf
> 
> Sure.
> 
> But not everybody got the memo[1] :P
> 
> I think it worth considering if we want to make large folio adoption
> smoother.
> 
> [1] https://www.reddit.com/r/bcachefs/comments/1vepk4a/comment/p1sn4v1/

Since I'm an idiot, I'm not inclined to be helpful.  But I think my
proposal does fix this; we call page_mkwrite() for each page fault and
then the filesystem knows which pages are actually dirty without having
to be told under the PTL when they can't reserve space.

2026-09-16.patch_summary: Proposal to track dirty pages at the PTE level for PTE-mapped mmap writes, aiming to improve performance and reduce unnecessary page faults.
